utterances.text: You know that after the letter was written by Judge Draganovic, that the Office of the Prosecutor then wrote a letter on your behalf requesting that you not be expelled from this third country until they had had an opportunity to interview you, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And someone from the OTP then did come and speak with you, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: No. That time, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, at some point you certainly spoke with representatives of the OTP, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes. When my status in the country where I was at was resolved, not thanks to The Hague Tribunal but thanks to a law which said that the person who was working, who was employed, can have their visa extended so that they could stay. So that was the way in which I resolved my pressing problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But the fact is the OTP had written a letter on your behalf, hadn't they?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he has already said yes that he's aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was the first person from the OTP that came to interview you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: I think that it was Ms. Sullivan. I think it was her. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And how long did that interview take? How much time was spent in that interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: The interview lasted maybe five or six hours, but I -- I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was it tape recorded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was or not. The only thing I know is that afterwards, that statement was read back to me and I signed it, but I don't know whether it was recorded or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, there was a lot took place before you signed your statement, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you be more precise, Mr. Ackerman, because that's a very vague question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It is. I'll just have to take the time and get there, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are in cross-examination, you can go as directly as you want.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, this interview, did you notice a recording machine, a tape recording machine, sitting there in front of you? Was there a microphone sitting there in front of you when you were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: I don't remember, to tell you the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You seem to have the ability to remember things from many years ago but can't remember that. Why is that? Why can't you remember if that statement was being recorded?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I can circumvent and shorten this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The microphone is on. I think I can short circuit this. I don't think the interview was, in fact, taped. I can check but it wouldn't have been a statement that was taped.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: At the time -- thank you. At the time you were dealing with the Office of the Prosecutor, you understood that the situation you might find yourself in would be enhanced if you could convince the Office of the Prosecutor that you were a very valuable witness, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: No. I'm here today, as I said, all of those problems that you're mentioning now in my life have now been resolved and all of the letters addressed to the Tribunal, in all of my letters addressed to the Tribunal, I said that I wanted to tell the truth of what happened to me in 1992. So, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, we are going to come to those in a minute. The reason you didn't want to be expelled from the country where you were was because you were afraid, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you were prepared to do anything that you could reasonably do to avoid being expelled, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, there was a time, for instance, wasn't there, when you wrote a letter to Mr. Mazhar Inayat, a handwritten letter. Do you remember writing that letter? It was a letter where you sent a copy of the videotape of [redacted] wedding.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You said to Mr. Inayat in that letter, didn't you, that -- and I know this is an error, you said that it was recorded in August of 1992, and I know you meant 1991. You said it shows military vehicles and helicopters which accompanied the column of wedding guests from the village of Kozarusa all the way to Kozarac. The -- the fact of that matter, sir, is this, isn't it? There was a convoy travelling that road at the same time you were, which was being escorted by helicopters, as convoys frequently are. It had nothing to do with that procession, did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: I've already said that we only understood that later. We didn't know what was happening. Two combat helicopters along the whole route. We didn't know that there was a military column behind us. But any way, they were going down the length of the whole column and then once we almost reached Kozarac, only then did we find out that this was an escort to the military convoy, and this is why I wrote that down. I didn't say that they either attacked or anything like that. They were escorting the column.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: At the time you wrote this letter, you knew that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what you said to Mr. Mazhar, whom you called Mr. Mazhar, was that the tape shows military vehicles and helicopters which accompanied the column of wedding guests from the village of Kozarusa all the way to Kozarac. Those are actually your words, aren't they? We can arrange for to you look at your letter, sir, if you want to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: There is no need. I've already told you that it was just as I had written it. Those two helicopters were escorting the military column but they were going along the whole length of that road, where the wedding column was also going. I didn't say anything other than that. I don't know what the real reason was, but anyway, those two helicopters followed the wedding procession all the way to almost -- almost all the way to the place where it turned off to go to the location where the wedding celebration was to be held.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, the letter that you wrote to Mr. Inayat, Mr. Mazhar Inayat that we have been talking about, is not dated. Can you tell us about when it was that you sent that letter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: It could have been perhaps in 1998 but I don't know exactly. I can't tell you that right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You then sent -- and I don't know whether this is before or after because again it's another undated letter but you wrote a letter to -- let me go back to the Mazhar letter for just a second and if you want to look at it, just please tell me and we'll make sure you get a chance to see it. It's the case, isn't it, that nowhere in that letter do you mention Mr. Brdjanin, or Mr. Brdjanin visiting Manjaca or anything at all about Mr. Brdjanin? It's not in that letter, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: It's true that at that point, I didn't even think about Mr. Brdjanin, nor did I charge him with anything. I've come here to confirm that I saw him, that during my stay at Manjaca, he did come there. I did not directly accuse Brdjanin, neither was that my intent at that time, nor is it my intent today. I'm here just to say that he was there, because I saw him and I've already explained that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, we are actually trying to finish today and if you could have answered that question, "No, I didn't mention Mr. Brdjanin," we would be a little further down the road and I'd appreciate it if you would just try to answer the question that I ask you. I want to go to -- the next letter in my packet of letters. This is a letter that you wrote to a gentleman by the name of Malik, Mr. Malik. I take it Mr. Malik is also an investigator for the Office of the Prosecutor, yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know whether he's an investigator, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this letter -- we need to go to private session for a moment, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go to private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, this statement -- this letter that you wrote to Malik, you talked about the weekend house and that whole series of events involving your confrontation in Omarska with Meakic and who it was that had destroyed your weekend house and all of that. That's what that letter was about, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And again, you know, don't you, that much of the contents of that letter is reproduced almost verbatim in your statement to the OTP, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And again, in that letter that you wrote to Malik you made no mention of Mr. Brdjanin, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The next one, on 29 November of 1999, you wrote another letter to Mr. Malik, and that's a letter where you tried to list the names of people who attended [redacted] wedding and who have disappeared and not been seen since. You remember writing that letter, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that's another letter in which you made no mention of Mr. Brdjanin, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You wrote another letter to Mr. Malik, sir, on 7 March of the year 2000. You told him about a person by the name of Nenad Penic who had been a guard in Omarska and how Penic had claimed that he had somehow protected you while you were there and you just wanted to make it clear I think that that was not the case, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you made it clear to Mr. Malik that were you very willing to testify at this Tribunal against people indicted for war crimes, and if you'd like, I'll quote the exact language because it might be important to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: There is no need.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: All right. So essentially what I suggested to you is correct, isn't it? And again in that letter you made no mention of Mr. Brdjanin, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your formal statement, sir, to the Prosecutor, the one of 29 October, 2001, as we have discussed, contains, to a great extent, the language from these various letters that you wrote to Mr. Malik, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And on 29 October, 2001, Mr. Brdjanin had been arrested and indicted by this Tribunal and when the Prosecutor investigator who talked to you and took this statement, when that person talked to you, they said to you, "It sure would be nice, considering all we've done for you, if you said something?"

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, objection sustained, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was it suggested to you by an investigator from the Prosecutor's offers that it would be helpful if you could mention something about Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: During your examination today, sir, you were asked about the visit of this delegation to Omarska that you had heard about. Do you remember talking about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I think you told us that the person who reported to you who the members were of that delegation, was a person named Ante Slutaj. I don't know how to spell that last name. Can you spell that last name for me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: S-L-U-T-A-J.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know where that person is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Not right now. I don't know where he is right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know that he's survived Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know who would know where he might be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at the photograph 1128.32, please. And while that photograph is being brought out, you said when you were talking about this visit of the delegation to Manjaca, that -- that you could hear, even though you didn't see, you -- your words were that you heard "fanatical chanting," correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And so you heard very clearly -- I'm sorry, I said Manjaca, and I meant Omarska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You could hear this chanting very clearly in room 15 where you were, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it was sufficiently loud, this singing and chanting, that anyone who was in the Omarska camp would have -- would have heard that noise that day, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: I don't know whether everybody would, but in room 15, one could hear it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Look at 1128.32, please. You see some white plastic bottles, it looks like, sitting up there on a shelf behind the people sitting there. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes. This is Manjaca camp and we received it from the ICRC when we got there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What are those? Those are water bottles, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes. When the ICRC registered us at Manjaca, each of us was given this water container and we went to the lake in Manjaca to fetch water in them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you also get cigarettes for those who smoked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT27
utterances.text: Yes. Even those who did not smoke. All of us got two cigarette packs, every two weeks, from the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, we need to stop within a minute's time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I hate to keep this person for the weekend for ten minutes, judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have other commitments after 6.30. We have been sitting for quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'll probably going to be quite embarrassed if I stop now by the five or ten minutes that I'll take on Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is no other option.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would imagine there is also some re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There might be, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we need to stop now. I'm afraid you have to stay in The Hague for the weekend because we can't conclude today. We will continue Monday morning, and that's it. The sitting is adjourned until Monday at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
